title: Email, payments and backups
intro: Only owners can change these. Saved passwords and keys are never shown again.
error: The request failed. Please try again.
conflict: Settings changed elsewhere. The latest saved settings are shown; review them and try again.
sandbox: This sandbox sends email to the demo outbox and takes payments through the demo’s Stripe test account. They can’t be changed here.
email.title: Email
email.sourceGym: Sends through your own SMTP service: {host}, port {port} ({security}), from {from}.
email.sourceInstall: Uses this install’s email settings (the SMTP_* values on the server).
email.sourceNone: No email service is set up: the gym can’t send email.
email.hint: Use an SMTP sending service such as Postmark, Brevo, or Amazon SES. The settings are saved only after a test email is accepted.
email.secure: Use TLS from the start (usually port 465)
email.confirmSignIn: I understand how people will sign in after this change
email.saved: Test email sent. The new email settings are saved.
email.testFailed: The test email failed. Check the settings and try again; nothing was saved.
email.remove: Remove and use the install’s settings
email.removeNone: Remove (the gym will have no email)
email.removed: The gym’s own email settings are removed.
email.onlySignIn: Email links are your only way to sign in, since your account has no password. Removing email would lock you out.
email.notConfigured: The gym has no email settings of its own.
payments.title: Payments
payments.notConfigured: Stripe isn’t connected: members can’t pay by card.
payments.webhookRegistered: Webhook endpoint registered: Stripe sends payment updates to this gym.
payments.locked: Members have Stripe customers, cards or payments, so a new key must be for the same Stripe account and mode.
payments.hint: Use a restricted key from your Stripe Dashboard with the permissions listed in setup. The key is checked, and the webhook endpoint is kept or replaced, before anything is saved.
payments.invalid: Enter a restricted key beginning with rk_test_ or rk_live_.
payments.saved: The new Stripe key is saved.
payments.missingPermission: Stripe refused one of the key’s permissions. Check them against the list in setup and try again.
payments.accountLocked: This key is for another Stripe account. Customers, cards and payments belong to the current one, so the key wasn’t saved.
payments.modeLocked: Customers, cards and payments exist in the current mode, so the key can’t switch between test and live.
payments.failed: Stripe couldn’t check the key. Check the key and your connection, then try again.
backups.title: Backups
backups.notConfigured: Backups aren’t set up. Updates refuse to run until they are.
backups.snapshotUnknown: The last snapshot couldn’t be checked.
backups.retention: Retention budget: {size}. Snapshots keep 24 hourly, 7 nightly, 4 weekly, and up to 2 pre-upgrade copies when space allows.
backups.changeWarning: After a change, new snapshots use the new destination and key, starting right after you confirm. Snapshots under the old key stay readable only with that key until retention removes them, so keep the old key until then. A new bucket starts empty, and the app no longer manages the old one: its snapshots stay there until you delete them.
backups.hint: Snapshots are encrypted before uploading. Only your backup private key can open them.
backups.pending: A new destination (bucket {bucket}) and key wait for you to confirm the private key. Until then, snapshots keep using the current settings.
backups.keyWarning: Save this private key somewhere safe, away from this server. It is shown once. Losing it means losing access to these backups.
backups.privateKey: Paste the private key you saved
backups.savedKey: I saved my private key somewhere safe
backups.confirmed: Backups now use the new destination and key.
backups.mismatch: That private key doesn’t match the new public key. Paste the key shown when you generated it.
backups.noPending: Generate a new backup key first.
backups.unreachable: The storage destination refused the request. Check the endpoint, region, bucket and access keys; nothing was changed.
